chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Pearl Bailey as vocalist in Cootie Williams's band
summary: Pearl Bailey was the band's only woman and not yet a star; Holmes credits a record with Hot Lips Page for launching her, though Vinson was the vocal star.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I just said Pearl Bailey was the vocalist with the Cootie Williams band, and that was before she become a big star. Most people didn't even know that she could sing. She was also a dancer, too. And it was nice working with her. She was the only woman with the band. There's really nothing too much to say.

The big vocal star in Cootie's band was Eddie Vinson. He was the big vocal star. He'd come into New York and be(?) layin' low. Pearl would be making records with Sinatra and different vocalists downtown. Her and Hot Lips Page made a record, "Baby, It's Cold Outside," and I think that's the one that started her off in the right direction. That record was Hot Lips Page, "Baby It's Cold Outside." And after that, she never looked back! She just turned out one record after another, and next thing I know she was a big star and had her name in the lights. She did all right.
But Cootie then more or less helped her get started?

Well, she was working with Cootie's band. She was a vocalist. I would say any time you work for anybody, they're helping you. You know? Sure. But she was not a big star. Eddie Vinson was the vocalist in the band. He was the big star. But he was a comedian and everything else. He was a star in his own right. He used to sing the
Blues, sing 'em good, and play the saxophone too. He could play. Yeah, he could really play. Mmm-hmm.
